events.title: Esquire publishes "Secrets of the Little Blue Box"
events.summary: Esquire magazine's October 1971 issue featured Ron Rosenbaum's article on phone phreaking — introducing blue boxes, Captain Crunch whistles, and blind hacker Joybubbles to mainstream America.
events.about: Phreakers exploited AT&T tone frequencies to route free long-distance calls — the spiritual ancestor of computer hacking culture. Steve Wozniak and Steve Jobs famously sold blue boxes before Apple; the article inspired a generation to explore systems by bending rules rather than breaking hardware.

narrative.whyChosen: The Esquire piece linked phone-system hacking to the culture that later built personal computing.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed how technical curiosity on networks could outpace corporate security assumptions.
narrative.problemSolved: This was exploratory subversion, not a product — it exposed that phone networks trusted in-band signaling anyone could mimic.
